workit install: Install or repair Workit on the named hosts only

usage: workit install --hosts=<h,…> [--preview | --yes]

--hosts takes the lowercase ids claude-code, codex, cursor, opencode, pi; --preview prints the files, config keys, host commands and notes and changes nothing; --yes installs them; with neither it asks at a terminal. It never changes the Workit config, a workspace or another host, and a host whose CLI is not on PATH shows a blocked row. Only the user applies it, in their own terminal: from an agent session the CLI runs --preview and refuses the rest, handing over the command, and a host may also ask about or deny the agent's call.

part.text:
`workit install` takes these flags (from `workit install --help`):

| Flag | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `--hosts=<h,…>` | **Required.** Comma-separated lowercase host ids from `claude-code`, `codex`, `cursor`, `opencode`, `pi` — only those named hosts are touched |
| `--preview` | Prints the files, config keys, host commands, and notes it would write; changes nothing |
| `--yes` | Actually performs the install/repair |
| `--` | Escape hatch for values starting with `-` (otherwise use `--flag=value`) |

Usage form: `workit install --hosts=<h,…> [--preview | --yes]`. With neither `--preview` nor `--yes` it prompts at a terminal.

Two constraints worth flagging: it never modifies the Workit config, a workspace, or a host you didn't name, and it is user-only in practice — from an agent session the CLI downgrades to `--preview` and refuses `--yes`, handing the full command back to you to run in your own terminal. Also, any host whose CLI isn't on `PATH` shows up as a blocked row rather than being silently skipped.

I only read the help text; nothing was installed or previewed.
